small_guidance:
- Add a GROUP_M block-swizzle (e.g. 8) for L2 reuse across N tiles in the same row group; M=1024, N=8192 means many N tiles per row, swizzling will help.
- Expand autotune with larger K tiles (BLOCK_K=64, 128) and num_stages=4 since K=8192 is large and the K-loop dominates; try (128,256,64) and (256,128,64) configs with num_warps=8.
- Convert weight to a transposed contiguous (K, N) buffer once in __init__ so the inner B load is along the contiguous N axis (stride_bn=1) instead of strided by K=8192 — this is the biggest single win available.
large_guidance:
- Pre-transpose weight to a (K, N) contiguous tensor stored as a buffer at init; the current kernel loads B with stride_bn=K (strided, non-coalesced along N), which on a 8192×8192 GEMM is the main bottleneck.
- Consider storing weight in fp16/bf16 (cast once at init) and doing tl.dot in fp16 with fp32 accumulator — RTX 4090 has much higher fp16 tensor-core throughput, and the loose 5e-2 tolerance easily accommodates it.
- Add a split-K or persistent-tile scheduler with GROUP_M swizzle; for M=1024, N=8192, K=8192 a persistent kernel with one program per SM that iterates output tiles maximizes weight reuse and reduces launch overhead.
